text: Loaded gpt2 on local-full (full precision (local)).

H1 (behaviour): On prompts 'The {subject} {prep} the {distractor}' where the distractor noun has the OPPOSITE number to the subject, gpt2 gives a higher logit to the verb form agreeing with the subject (' is' vs ' are'). Dataset: 16 noun items x 2 (sg subject + pl distractor; pl subject + sg distractor) = 32 clean prompts; corrupt = same prompt with subject number flipped (distractor unchanged, same token count). Metric: logit_diff(correct verb - incorrect verb) at final position. Against H1: mean logit diff <= 0 or accuracy near 50%, or clean/corrupt token lengths misaligned.
Baseline for H1: subject-verb agreement across an opposite-number distractor

E0001 (local-full): logit diff (correct - incorrect verb) is positive on 32/32 clean prompts (mean +3.34, min +1.46) and negative on 32/32 corrupt prompts scored with clean labels (mean -4.36). So the model prefers the subject-agreeing verb form over the distractor-agreeing one in every pair. Note: top-1 'accuracy' is only 0.19 because the argmax token is often something other than is/are (e.g. ' "', ','); the behaviour is a relative preference between verb forms, not top-1 prediction. Clean and corrupt aligned (no length error).
Supported by E0001: 32/32 clean prompts have positive logit diff; with the caveat that is/are is often not the top-1 token.

H2 (where): The subject's number is read at the subject token (pos 2) in early layers and must be moved to the final position (the distractor noun, pos 5) by attention heads in middle layers, since only the subject token differs between clean and corrupt. Prediction for attribution patching (corrupt->clean): effect concentrated at the subject position in early layers and at the final position in later layers, with a small number of heads carrying the transfer. Against H2: effect spread diffusely over all positions/heads, or large effects at positions other than subject and final (e.g. preposition / 'the') would mean number is relayed through intermediate tokens.
Screen for H2: where (layer/position/head) does subject number matter?

E0002 attribution screen (local-full, first-order estimate only, normalised effect; positions: 0=BOS,1=The,2=subject,3=prep,4=the,5=distractor/final). Top heads: 7.4 (0.16), 8.5 (0.145), 10.9 (0.13), 6.0 (0.07), 10.5 (0.07), 11.10 (0.05), 5.2 (0.03). Resid: final pos dominates from layer 8 on; subject pos 2 moderate; the PREPOSITION pos 3 has estimated effect in layers 5-7 (0.11-0.19), which H2 did not predict. MLPs 8-11 at the final position have large estimates (0.07-0.29). Caveat: the estimate is badly non-conservative (resid_pre.0 @ subject is -0.008 although it must be ~1.0 exactly), so nothing here is trusted until activation patching confirms.
Exact test of H2: resid_pre by layer x position. Against H2: substantial effect at pos 3/4 (relay through intermediate tokens).

E0003 exact resid_pre patching (local-full, corrupt->clean denoise, effect = fraction of clean-corrupt gap restored). Subject pos 2: 1.00 (L0-2), 0.94 (L3), 0.73 (L4), 0.46 (L5), 0.42 (L6), 0.39 (L7), 0.35 (L8), 0.24 (L9-10), 0.03 (L11). Preposition pos 3: 0.06 (L3), 0.28 (L4), 0.49 (L5), 0.43 (L6), 0.31 (L7), 0.10 (L8), 0.03 (L9). 'the' pos 4: <=0.06 everywhere. Final pos 5: 0.03 (L5), 0.07 (L6), 0.18 (L7), 0.55 (L8), 0.75 (L9), 0.76 (L10), 0.97 (L11). Reading: (a) layers 3-4 copy about half of the subject-number signal onto the preposition token; (b) layers 7-8 move it to the final position (from prep and/or subject); (c) layer 10 moves a remaining ~0.2 from the subject token to the final position. The determiner 'the' carries almost nothing.

Revised by E0003: number is not only moved subject->final. About half of the signal is first relayed onto the preposition token (pos 3) in layers 3-4, then read from there in layers 7-8; the direct subject->final part is carried mostly in layers 7-8 and again at layer 10. The 'against' condition (large effect at the preposition) occurred, so the single-hop version of H2 is wrong.

H3 (which heads): the movement to the final position is carried by a few heads flagged by the screen: 7.4, 8.5 (layers 7-8 step) and 10.9, 10.5 (layer 10 step), plus smaller 6.0, 11.10. Exact head-output patching (corrupt->clean) should give each of these a clearly larger effect than every other head. Against H3: exact effects of these heads near zero, or other heads (not in the screen) dominating. The early prep-relay heads (layers 3-4) are not identified by the screen, so the head sweep should also reveal which layer 3-4 heads have effect.
Exact test of H3: per-head output patching corrupt->clean

E0004 exact head-output patching (local-full, corrupt->clean, fraction restored): 7.4 0.252, 8.5 0.208, 10.9 0.171, 6.0 0.114, 10.5 0.077, 4.3 0.057, 11.10 0.055, 5.2 0.050, 3.7 0.022, 4.11 0.018; largest negative 6.5 -0.025; all other heads |effect| < 0.02. The six heads named in H3 are indeed the top ones, in the same order as the screen; new: 4.3 and 5.2 (not predicted). No single layer 3-4 head explains the 0.49 that arrives at the preposition by layer 5, so that relay is either distributed over heads or involves MLPs: open.
Supported by E0004 for the named heads (7.4, 8.5, 10.9, 6.0, 10.5, 11.10 are the top exact effects, with 4.3 and 5.2 added). Not yet shown: where each head attends and which position it writes to.

H4 (layer-level bookkeeping): (a) attention layers 3-4 write the number signal at the preposition position (pos 3); (b) attention layers 6-8 and 10 write it at the final position (pos 5); (c) MLPs at the final position in layers 8-11 matter as flagged by the screen (they would turn 'subject is plural' into verb-form logits). Test: exact attn_out and mlp_out patching by layer x position. Against: (a) fails if attn_out L3-4 @ pos 3 effects are ~0 (then MLP or something else does the relay); (c) fails if mlp_out @ pos 5 exact effects are < 0.05 everywhere.
H4 a,b: attn_out by layer x position
H4 c: mlp_out by layer x position

E0005/E0006 exact layer-level patching (local-full, all positions at once; the tool did not split by position, so the positional part of H4 is untested here). attn_out: L10 0.285, L7 0.277, L8 0.173, L6 0.099, L5 0.061, L11 0.054, L4 0.043, L3 0.041, L2 0.027, L9 0.013. mlp_out: L0 0.988 (the subject token's identity/number passes through MLP0), L10 0.332, L11 0.243, L9 0.220, L8 0.127, L1-7 each <= 0.035. So late MLPs 8-11 matter (H4c holds at layer level), and attention layers 3-4 have only ~0.04 each although the preposition residual carries 0.49 by layer 5 (E0003): single-layer denoising effects are not additive here, the prep relay is spread over layers 2-5.

H5 (what the mover heads read): at the final position, heads 7.4, 8.5, 6.0 attend to the subject noun (pos 2) and/or the preposition (pos 3), and 10.9, 10.5, 11.10 attend to the subject noun (pos 2), since E0003 shows the subject residual still matters until layer 10 while the prep residual stops mattering after layer 8. Test: attention from query pos 5 to key pos 2 and to key pos 3 for all heads. Against: these heads put < 0.1 attention on pos 2 and pos 3 (then they are not moving number from those tokens; they would be transforming information already at the final position).
H5: attention final(5) -> subject(2), all heads
H5: attention final(5) -> preposition(3), all heads
Prep relay: attention preposition(3) -> subject(2), all heads (which early heads copy number onto the preposition?)

Attention patterns (local-full, mean over 32 clean prompts). From the FINAL position (5): 6.0 -> subj 0.045 / prep 0.332; 7.4 -> subj 0.067 / prep 0.209; 8.5 -> subj 0.119 / prep 0.180; 5.2 -> subj 0.025 / prep 0.193; 10.9 -> subj 0.220 / prep 0.128; 10.5 -> subj 0.243 / prep 0.075; 11.10 -> subj 0.245 / prep 0.074 (E0007, E0008). So the layer 5-8 heads look mostly at the preposition, the layer 10-11 heads mostly at the subject noun; all put most of their remaining weight on BOS, so these are modest attention weights (0.2-0.33), not sharp pointers. From the PREPOSITION (3) to the subject (2): 4.11 1.00, 2.9 0.80, 2.2 0.71, 3.7 0.70, 4.3 0.67, 4.1 0.47, 2.4 0.47, 3.3 0.45 (E0009): many early heads look from the preposition back at the subject, consistent with a distributed relay. Attention alone is correlational; path patching needed.

Supported with a refinement (E0007, E0008): none of the mover heads falls below the 0.1 threshold on both positions. Layer 5-8 heads (6.0, 7.4, 8.5, 5.2) prefer the preposition; layer 10-11 heads (10.9, 10.5, 11.10) prefer the subject. Weights are moderate (0.18-0.33).

H6 (two-hop path): early heads that attend prep->subject (2.2, 2.9, 3.7, 4.3, 4.11) write subject number onto the preposition, and the mid heads 6.0, 7.4, 8.5 read it there through their VALUE input. Test: path patching senders [2.2, 2.9, 3.7, 4.3, 4.11] -> receivers [6.0, 7.4, 8.5] input v. Prediction: effect clearly > 0 (order 0.1, given the non-additivity seen in E0005). Against: effect < 0.02, meaning the mid heads get number via another route (MLPs at the prep, or directly from the subject token).
H6: early prep->subject heads -> value input of 6.0/7.4/8.5
Direct path of mover heads to logits (vs. total effect in E0004): which heads write the verb form directly and which act through later components?

Path patching (local-full, per sender, fraction restored). E0010 early heads -> VALUE input of {6.0, 7.4, 8.5}: 4.3 0.039, 3.7 0.025, 4.11 0.014, 2.9 0.012, 2.2 0.007 (sum 0.097). Compared with their total effects in E0004 (4.3 0.057, 3.7 0.022, 4.11 0.018, 2.9 0.011, 2.2 0.008), most of what these early heads do is mediated by the values of 6.0/7.4/8.5. But the amounts are small: the five heads together account for ~0.1, far less than the 0.49 the preposition residual carries (E0003). E0011 direct path to logits vs total effect (E0004): 10.9 0.107 of 0.171; 7.4 0.079 of 0.252; 8.5 0.064 of 0.208; 11.10 0.046 of 0.055; 10.5 0.046 of 0.077; 6.0 0.046 of 0.114; 5.2 0.029 of 0.050; 4.3 0.007 of 0.057. So the layer 10-11 heads write the verb preference mostly directly, whereas 6.0/7.4/8.5 act about two thirds INDIRECTLY, through later components (late MLPs and/or late heads).

Revised by E0010: the path early prep-heads -> value of 6.0/7.4/8.5 exists and carries most of those early heads' effect (4.3 and 3.7 pass the 0.02 bar; 4.11, 2.9, 2.2 do not), but it explains only ~0.1 of the gap. The relay onto the preposition is distributed; no small set of early heads carries it. I will not claim specific early relay heads as necessary circuit members beyond 4.3 and 3.7 as the largest contributors.

H7 (indirect route of mid heads): the indirect two thirds of 6.0/7.4/8.5 goes through late MLPs at the final position (MLP 8-11 had exact effects 0.13-0.33 in E0006) rather than through the late heads' queries. Test 1: path patching senders [6.0, 7.4, 8.5] -> receivers [10.5, 10.9, 11.10] input q. If H7 is right this is small (< 0.03 per sender); if instead it is > 0.05 per sender, the late heads depend on the mid heads (a head->head chain) and H7 is wrong in that part. Test 2 (next): mean-ablating MLPs 8-11 should remove a large part of the logit diff.
H7 test 1: mid heads -> query of late heads
H7 test 2: mean-ablation sweep over MLPs
Necessity screen: mean-ablation sweep over all heads (do the heads found by denoising also matter when knocked out? any head denoising missed?)

E0012 (local-full) path patching mid heads -> QUERY of {10.5, 10.9, 11.10}: 6.0 0.001, 7.4 -0.001, 8.5 0.000, 5.2 0.000. The late heads do not depend on the mid heads through their queries: the two groups act in parallel, not as a chain. E0013 mean-ablation sweep of MLPs (reference = clean-set mean; clean metric 3.34): mlp0 -> 1.87, mlp8 -> 2.11, mlp10 -> 2.14, mlp11 -> 2.38, mlp9 -> 2.96; mlp1-7 change by <= +0.18 (slightly up). E0014 mean-ablation sweep of heads: 7.4 -> 2.67 (-0.67), 10.9 -> 2.78 (-0.56), 8.5 -> 2.85 (-0.49), 6.0 -> 3.10 (-0.24), 10.5 -> 3.11 (-0.23), 11.10 -> 3.16 (-0.18), 5.2 -> 3.23 (-0.11), 4.3 -> 3.25 (-0.09), 7.8 -> 3.27 (-0.07); every other head |change| < 0.06. Knock-out ranking matches the denoising ranking (E0004), no hidden head. No single component is necessary on its own: the largest single knock-outs remove 20% (head 7.4) and 37-44% (mlp8, mlp10, mlp0).

H8 (joint necessity and the MLP link): (a) Jointly mean-ablating the 8 heads {4.3, 5.2, 6.0, 7.4, 8.5, 10.5, 10.9, 11.10} removes most of the logit diff (prediction: metric falls below 1.0 from 3.34, i.e. > 70% lost). Against: metric stays > 2.0 (then other heads compensate or carry the signal and the head set is incomplete). (b) the indirect effect of 6.0/7.4/8.5 flows into MLPs 8-11: path patching senders [6.0, 7.4, 8.5] with MLPs as receiver, if the tool supports an MLP receiver; otherwise this stays an inference from E0011 + E0012 + E0013 and is reported as such.
H8a: joint mean ablation of the 8 candidate heads

Control for H8a: joint mean ablation of 8 heads I claim do NOT matter (incl. 11.8 and 1.10 which attend strongly final->subject, and 2.2/3.3 which attend prep->subject). Prediction: metric stays > 3.0.

E0015 (local-full): joint mean ablation of the 8 heads {4.3, 5.2, 6.0, 7.4, 8.5, 10.5, 10.9, 11.10} drops the logit diff from 3.34 to 0.21 (6% of clean). E0016 control: joint mean ablation of 8 other heads {7.8, 6.5, 2.2, 8.7, 9.3, 3.3, 1.10, 11.8}, chosen to include heads with strong final->subject or prep->subject attention (11.8 0.40, 1.10 0.22, 2.2 0.71, 3.3 0.45), leaves it at 3.35 (100%). So attention to the subject is not sufficient to matter; the 8 named heads are jointly necessary on this dataset. An attempted path patch with MLPs as receiver failed (KeyError 'heads': the tool only accepts head receivers; no experiment id was issued), so the 'mid heads -> late MLPs' link cannot be measured directly here.

(a) supported by E0015 (0.21 < 1.0) with control E0016 (3.35). (b) NOT tested: MLP receivers unsupported in path_patching. It remains an inference: mid heads are 2/3 indirect (E0011), not via late-head queries (E0012), and MLPs 8-11 each matter when ablated (E0013).

H9 (what is represented where): the subject's number becomes linearly decodable at the FINAL position only once the mover heads have written it, i.e. probe accuracy at the last token for 'subject is plural' is near chance in layers 0-5 and rises to > 0.9 by layers 8-9 (matching E0003 where the final-position residual effect goes 0.07 -> 0.55 -> 0.75 over layers 6-9). Data: the 64 prompts (clean + corrupt), in which subject number and distractor number are crossed (all 4 combinations equally often), so the probe cannot use the distractor's own number. Against: accuracy already high in layers 0-4 (then the info is at the final position before the movers act, contradicting the patching picture), or never above the control.
H9: probe 'subject is plural' at the final token, per layer; distractor number crossed

E0017 (local-full) linear probe for 'subject is plural' at the final token (64 prompts, 44 train / 20 test, subject and distractor number crossed). Held-out accuracy by resid_post layer 0..11: 0.15, 0.15, 0.40, 0.60, 0.70, 0.70, 0.80, 0.85, 0.85, 0.85, 1.00, 1.00. Shuffled-label control ranges 0.25-0.65. With only 20 test prompts each step is 0.05 and the control itself swings by +-0.2, so this is weak evidence: the trend (not decodable in layers 0-2, perfectly decodable from layer 10) agrees with the patching picture, but the specific prediction '> 0.9 by layer 8-9' was not met (0.85), and the below-chance 0.15 in layers 0-1 shows the small-sample probe is unreliable there.

Revised by E0017: direction of the prediction holds (chance or below early, 1.0 at layers 10-11) but the threshold was missed at layers 8-9 (0.85) and the probe is underpowered (n_test = 20). Treated as weak corroboration only; no claim rests on it alone.

H10 (a number direction is causally sufficient at the final position): the difference of mean residuals (plural-subject prompts minus singular-subject prompts, distractor number balanced) at the final position in layers ~8-10 is a 'subject is plural' direction. Adding it at the final position on singular-subject prompts should push the logit diff (' is' - ' are') from positive to negative, and subtracting it should increase it, monotonically in alpha. Against: no monotone change, or the sign never flips at alphas of the order of the natural difference (alpha ~ 1-2 in units of the mean difference).
H10 step 1: plural-subject minus singular-subject direction per layer (distractor balanced)
H10 step 2: add the plural-subject direction at resid_post.9 on singular-subject prompts; metric = logit(is) - logit(are)

H10 rerun at natural scale: E0019 used relative scale where alpha=1 is the full residual norm (154), ~8x the natural plural-singular difference (norm 19.75 = 0.126 relative at resid_post.9). alpha=0.126 is one natural unit.

E0018 (local-full) diff-of-means direction 'plural subject minus singular subject' at the final token (32 vs 32, distractor balanced): norm grows 0.9 (L0) -> 7.7 (L6) -> 15.6 (L8) -> 19.8 (L9) -> 37.4 (L10) -> 55.6 (L11); as a held-out classifier the raw mean-difference is poor until late (accuracy 0.34-0.47 through L9, 0.66 at L10, 0.84 at L11), so it is not a clean read-out direction. Steering is the causal test. E0019 used the tool's relative scale (alpha 1 = full residual norm 154.7, about 8x the natural difference) and is therefore an overdose: metric (is - are on 16 singular-subject prompts) 3.26 -> -19.1 at alpha 1. E0020 at natural scale (alpha 0.126 = one plural-minus-singular unit at resid_post.9): alpha -0.126: 5.43; -0.063: 4.62; 0: 3.26; +0.063: -0.17; +0.126: -3.77; +0.252: -7.78. Monotone, and one natural unit flips the preference to about the value plural-subject prompts have (corrupt mean -4.36 in E0001). Caveat: I passed pos=-1 but the output does not confirm whether steering was restricted to the final position.
Supported by E0020 (monotone, sign flips at one natural unit). E0019 not used as evidence for natural-scale behaviour (8x overdose). Position restriction unconfirmed.

H11 (who writes the answer): the direct write along the (correct - incorrect verb) unembedding direction comes mainly from heads 10.9, 7.4, 8.5 (largest direct path effects in E0011) and no head outside the 8-head set has a comparable direct contribution. Test: direct_logit_attribution on the clean prompts. Against: a head outside the set with a direct contribution as large as 10.9's, or the named heads having ~0 direct attribution.
H11: direct logit attribution per head/MLP along correct-minus-incorrect verb direction

E0021 (local-full) direct logit attribution along (correct - incorrect verb), clean prompts, logit units: 10.9 +0.434, 7.4 +0.314, 8.5 +0.230, 10.5 +0.176, 6.0 +0.169, 11.10 +0.169, 5.2 +0.106; largest outside the set: 0.5 -0.054, 6.5 -0.047, 7.8 +0.031. All heads together contribute 1.52 of the 3.34 logit diff, the seven named heads 1.60 (other heads net slightly negative). The remaining ~1.8 (about 55%) is written directly by non-head components (MLPs / embeddings), consistent with late MLPs 8-11 mattering in E0006/E0013. H11 holds: no outside head has a comparable direct write.
Supported by E0021.

H12 (the algorithm, to be verified on held-out nouns): predict(prompt) = ' are' if the subject noun (token 2) is plural else ' is', ignoring the distractor. Circuit = heads {4.3, 5.2, 6.0, 7.4, 8.5, 10.5, 10.9, 11.10} + MLPs {0, 8, 9, 10, 11}. Held-out set: 24 NEW subject nouns, new distractor nouns and partly new prepositions (in, at, for, on, over), 48 clean/corrupt pairs, none used in E0001-E0021. Predictions: (1) the model's preferred verb form matches predict() on > 90% of prompts; (2) mean-ablating the circuit removes most of the logit diff; (3) mean-ablating everything outside the circuit keeps most of it; (4) a random same-size set does much less than the circuit. Against: any of these failing; (3) is the riskiest, since E0003/E0010 showed the early relay onto the preposition is distributed over components I did NOT put in the circuit.
subject-number agreement across a distractor (held-out nouns): not-verified. At least one check failed; the explanation is partial or wrong. See the numbers.

V0001 (local-full, 48 held-out pairs, new subject nouns): NOT verified. (1) Behaviour generalises: clean logit diff 3.23 on held-out nouns (3.34 on the development set). (2) Agreement check FAILED: 0.167. The tool compares predict() with the model's top-1 token, and the model's top-1 after these prompts is usually ',', ' "', ' were' etc.; is/are is top-1 on only 17% of prompts. predict() matches the grammatical ground truth on 100%, but the tool does not report how often the model's is-vs-are preference matches it, so the algorithm describes a relative preference between two verb forms, not the model's next-token output. (3) Circuit ablated (8 heads + MLP 0, 8-11, mean, corrupt reference): logit diff -0.30 (-9% of clean) -> necessity PASSES; 3 random same-size sets leave 96-106%. (4) Everything else ablated: 0.92 (28% of clean), threshold 0.7 -> sufficiency FAILS. As anticipated in H12, the 13 components are necessary but not sufficient: something outside them (candidates: the distributed early prep-relay heads, MLPs 1-7) carries or prepares the signal.

Revised by V0001: predictions (2) and (4) held, (1) failed as measured (top-1 agreement 0.17; the behaviour is a preference between verb forms, not top-1), (3) failed (28% survives on the circuit alone). The 13-component circuit is necessary, not sufficient.

H13 (what is missing): the sufficiency gap comes from (A) non-circuit attention heads, mainly the early layer 2-5 heads that relay number onto the preposition, and/or (B) MLPs 1-7. Tests on the development set, joint mean ablation: (A) all 136 non-circuit heads with all MLPs intact; (B) MLPs 1-7 with all heads intact. Whichever group drops the logit diff well below the clean 3.34 holds the missing part. Against H13-A: (A) leaves > 80%; against H13-B: (B) leaves > 80%. If both leave > 80% the gap is an interaction that only appears when both are removed.
H13-B: joint mean ablation of MLPs 1-7
H13-A1: joint mean ablation of all 70 non-circuit heads in layers 0-5
H13-A2: joint mean ablation of all 66 non-circuit heads in layers 6-11

Joint mean ablations on the development set (local-full, clean metric 3.34). E0024: all 66 non-circuit heads in layers 6-11 -> 3.42 (103%): none of the late heads outside the six movers matters, even jointly. E0023: all 70 non-circuit heads in layers 0-5 -> 2.82 (84%): the early heads together carry only ~16%; the relay onto the preposition is NOT mainly a job of early attention heads outside 4.3/5.2. E0022: MLPs 1-7 jointly -> 1.97 (59%), although each of them alone changed the metric by <= 0.18 (E0013): the early/mid MLPs are redundant individually but matter as a group.

Revised by E0022-E0024: H13-B holds (MLPs 1-7 jointly: 59%, below the 80% bar), H13-A is rejected by its own criterion (early non-circuit heads leave 84%, late ones 103%). The missing part of the circuit is mainly the group of MLPs 1-7, not extra heads.

H14 (revised circuit): attention side = only 8 of 144 heads {4.3, 5.2, 6.0, 7.4, 8.5, 10.5, 10.9, 11.10}; MLP side = MLPs are needed broadly. Tests: (i) joint mean ablation of ALL 136 non-circuit heads at once with every MLP intact should keep >= 70% of the logit diff (against: < 50%, then early and late non-circuit heads interact and the head set is incomplete). (ii)/(iii) to see whether the MLP group can be narrowed: joint ablation of MLPs 1-3 vs MLPs 4-7; if one block leaves > 90% it can be dropped from the circuit.
H14-ii: joint mean ablation MLPs 1-3
H14-iii: joint mean ablation MLPs 4-7

E0025 (local-full): joint mean ablation of MLPs 1-3 -> 3.58 (107%). E0026: MLPs 4-7 -> 3.09 (92%). But MLPs 1-7 together -> 1.97 (59%, E0022). Each block is dispensable when the other is present; removing both costs 41%. So neither block can be dropped from the circuit by the 90% criterion taken jointly: the early/mid MLPs are a redundant group. I did not test (i) all 136 non-circuit heads at once on the development set; that is tested directly on held-out prompts in the next verification.

H15 (second verification, fresh held-out set): circuit = 8 heads {4.3, 5.2, 6.0, 7.4, 8.5, 10.5, 10.9, 11.10} + all 12 MLPs (20 of 156 components; the claim is about attention sparsity: 136 of 144 heads are not needed). New prompts with 24 subject nouns used in neither E0001-E0026 nor V0001. Predictions: circuit ablated -> logit diff near or below 0; everything else (136 heads) ablated -> >= 70% of clean survives; random same-size control ablation does far less damage than the circuit. Expected failure that I will NOT tune away: the top-1 agreement check, because is/are is rarely the top-1 token (V0001: 17%). Against: sufficiency < 70% again.
agreement across distractor: 8 heads + all MLPs (fresh held-out nouns): not-verified. At least one check failed; the explanation is partial or wrong. See the numbers.

V0002 (local-full, 48 fresh held-out pairs; a first submission failed with a token-length error because one noun was multi-token, I replaced the risky nouns before any result was seen). Circuit = 8 heads + all 12 MLPs. Causal check PASSES: everything else ablated (all 136 other heads, mean, corrupt reference) -> logit diff 2.30 = 73.7% of clean 3.12 (threshold 70%); circuit ablated -> -0.08 (-2.5%); random same-size ablations leave 96-100%. Caveat: 'circuit ablated' here removes all MLPs, which would break almost any behaviour, so the informative necessity numbers are the head-only ones (E0015: 8 heads -> 6%; V0001: 8 heads + 5 MLPs -> -9%). Agreement check FAILS again: top-1 agreement 0.167 (model's top-1 is ',', ' were', \"'s\", ' at' ...), algorithm vs grammatical ground truth 1.0. Tool status: not-verified.

H16 (preference-level agreement on held-out prompts): although is/are is seldom top-1, the model's PREFERENCE between ' is' and ' are' follows predict() on the V0002 held-out prompts: per-prompt logit diff (correct - incorrect, where 'correct' is exactly what predict() returns) is positive on >= 90% of the 48 clean prompts and negative on >= 90% of the 48 corrupt prompts when scored with clean labels. Against: fewer than 90% in either set.
